name: What kinds of ADUs can I build (garage conversion, detached, above garage, JADU), and how do they compare?

mainEntity.name: What kinds of ADUs can I build (garage conversion, detached, above garage, JADU), and how do they compare?

acceptedAnswer.text:
The main ADU types are **garage conversions, attached ADUs, detached ADUs, above‑garage ADUs, and JADUs** (junior ADUs). Each comes with different costs, rules, and ideal use cases.

Choosing the right type depends on your site, budget, and whether you prioritize rental income, privacy, or speed of construction. In LA County, you can often combine one full ADU with one JADU on single‑family lots.

Key factors:
- Garage conversions: often cheapest, but sacrifice parking/storage
- Detached ADUs: best privacy, typically highest cost and longest build
- Above‑garage ADUs: great for small lots, but add structural and fire complexities
- JADUs: smaller (usually up to 500 sq ft) using existing space, limited by shared facilities

Map your property and overlay each option’s footprint, access path, and impact on your yard. Then compare total cost, timeline, and long‑term flexibility rather than just the initial construction price.

An ADU specialist can help you test multiple layout options so you can see which type aligns best with your goals.
acceptedAnswer.description: You can typically choose among garage conversions, attached ADUs, detached backyard cottages, above‑garage ADUs, and smaller JADUs. Garage conversions and JADUs are usually cheaper and faster; detached and above‑garage ADUs cost more but offer better privacy and layout flexibility. The best choice depends on your lot, budget, and long‑term plans.
